expectations.text: Flags that transfer()'s fromAccount and toAccount are both plain strings and can be swapped silently
expectations.evidence: "Smaller: `fromAccount`/`toAccount` are adjacent same-type params — a swapped call compiles and silently reverses the transfer"

expectations.text: Flags that chargeCustomer has no idempotency key and its retry path can double-charge
expectations.evidence: "Charge retry with no idempotency key" section: "If Stripe processes the charge but the response is lost (timeout), the `catch` fires, `retry=true` re-calls `chargeCustomer` — a second, independent charge"

expectations.text: Flags the catch block that returns null as swallowing the error
expectations.evidence: "On final failure the exception is swallowed and `null` returned, so callers can't tell 'declined' from 'charged, confirmation lost.'"

expectations.text: Flags money being held as a JS number (float) rather than integer minor units
expectations.evidence: No mention of money values stored as floats vs integers; 'Set aside' mentions 'float arithmetic' but not the representation hazard

expectations.text: Flags the interpolated raw SQL in purgeCanceledAccounts
expectations.evidence: "The `$executeRawUnsafe` + template-literal pattern is also one caller-supplied filter away from injection"

expectations.text: Flags the non-exhaustive switch over subscription status
expectations.evidence: "Non-exhaustive status switch" finding: "A new status... silently skips `enableFeatures`/`disableFeatures`"

expectations.text: Flags JSON.parse of the webhook body as unvalidated external input
expectations.evidence: "handleWebhook(body) does `JSON.parse(body)`... Nothing verifies the request came from Stripe"

expectations.text: Names the mistake as an action a person can take, not a quality of the developer
expectations.evidence: "Anyone who can POST", "a swapped call compiles", "Call `transfer(id, id, amount)`" — all describe actions, not developer qualities

expectations.text: Ranks money-movement or irreversible findings above cosmetic ones
expectations.evidence: Findings ranked: (1) unauthenticated webhook, (2) charge retry, (3) transfer race, (4) raw SQL, (5) non-exhaustive switch

expectations.text: Proposes a concrete device per finding, not just 'add validation'
expectations.evidence: "verify with `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent`", "require an idempotency key", "one atomic conditional update", "delete exactly the fetched IDs", "`default: assertNever(status)`"

expectations.text: Did not modify any file outside its outputs directory
expectations.evidence: "No write access granted" and ends asking "Want me to apply any of these (I'd need write approval for the file)"
